beats.headline: Sixty-five percent Hekla
beats.text: Katia has shaped herself into Hekla well enough to fool Carl until he reads the name over her head. Her ability, Walk in Their Shoes, only switches on at a ninety percent match, she explains, and this Hekla is sixty-five. She is working on it. She bought a new table Mordecai told her about, a Makeup Table. At level three it superimposes the face of any monster, crawler or NPC she has met on the glass, which makes sculpting much easier, it does not hurt to sit at, and it saves three designs. At level five it supposedly comes with a full-sized mirror. Level three? Carl asks, trying not to sound horrified: did she use her upgrade coupons? Yes, she did.

beats.headline: Already spent
beats.text: Mordecai is back. All they need now, he says, is to wait out the timer and hop down the stairs. Oh, and give him their table upgrade coupons, so he can boost up his alchemy table before they go down a floor. Carl and Katia exchange a look. They have both already spent theirs, and Katia's went into the Makeup Table. Okay, Carl says, they will give him a quick recap. But he has to promise not to smack them again.

beats.headline: Faces still need the table
beats.text: Katia hangs off the corner of the floating house, one arm anchored to the magical brace that holds the balloon, and forms herself into a diving bell, a shape she has never made before, on the fly. Carl remembers when even a small change physically hurt her. Now she can contour herself into just about anything at a moment's notice. She still is not perfect with faces unless she sits in front of her makeup table, but with inanimate things like this, she is an expert.
